_comment: Shared corpus for the :name -> $n statement compiler used by the Postgres sink. Mirrored verbatim into drakkar-go, so both backends compile operator-authored SQL to the same text with the same parameter order.

ok.sql: UPDATE t SET a = :a WHERE id = :id
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE t SET a = $1 WHERE id = $2

ok.case: repeated name collapses to one index and one param
ok.sql: UPDATE t SET a = :v, b = :v WHERE id = :id
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE t SET a = $1, b = $1 WHERE id = $2

ok.case: cast operator is not a placeholder
ok.sql: UPDATE t SET a = :v::text WHERE id = :id
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE t SET a = $1::text WHERE id = $2

ok.case: colon inside a string literal is untouched
ok.sql: UPDATE t SET note = 'a:b' WHERE id = :id
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE t SET note = 'a:b' WHERE id = $1

ok.sql: UPDATE t SET note = 'it''s :nope' WHERE id = :id
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE t SET note = 'it''s :nope' WHERE id = $1

ok.case: colon inside a quoted identifier is untouched

ok.sql: UPDATE t SET body = $$:nope$$ WHERE id = :id
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE t SET body = $$:nope$$ WHERE id = $1

ok.sql: UPDATE t SET body = $tag$:nope$tag$ WHERE id = :id
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE t SET body = $tag$:nope$tag$ WHERE id = $1

ok.sql: /* outer /* :nope */ still */ UPDATE t SET a = :a
ok.expected_sql: /* outer /* :nope */ still */ UPDATE t SET a = $1

ok.case: array slice colon is copied verbatim
ok.sql: UPDATE t SET a = arr[1:3] WHERE id = :id
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE t SET a = arr[1:3] WHERE id = $1

ok.case: assignment operator colon is copied verbatim
non-ASCII digit after a dollar is not a positional placeholder
expression and guard, the motivating case for operator-authored SQL
ok.sql: UPDATE jobs SET status = :status, attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE id = :id AND status = 'pending'
ok.expected_sql: UPDATE jobs SET status = $1, attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE id = $2 AND status = 'pending'

errors.sql: UPDATE t SET a = $1 WHERE id = :id
